html:
In 1661 and 1662 the Ming loyalist Koxinga drove the Dutch out of Taiwan and set up the first Han Chinese state on the island, the Kingdom of Tungning. Settlers from Fujian followed and began filling the western plains.

Koxinga, or Zheng Chenggong, was the son of a Chinese merchant and pirate and a Japanese mother. When the Qing conquered China he led a fleet and army in the name of the fallen Ming. After a failed attack on Nanjing in 1659 he needed a base. He besieged the Dutch at Fort Zeelandia, who surrendered in early 1662. He died a few months later.

His son and grandson ruled Taiwan and traded across the seas from Japan to Southeast Asia. To starve them, the Qing forced people away from the mainland coast in the Great Clearance. In 1683 a Qing fleet took Taiwan.

The Zheng years brought Han farmers to Taiwan in numbers for the first time, pushing back the island's Indigenous peoples. That shift shaped Taiwan from then on.
